docs.title: Comprehensive Assessment
docs.text:
Content Note

The comprehensive assessment serves as an important basis for departments to evaluate scholarships and honors. Department-specific details may vary. This page is compiled using the School of Computer Science and Technology, Class of 2022 comprehensive assessment standards (revised March 2023) as an example, for reference only.

docs.title: Score Composition
docs.text:
The comprehensive assessment totals 100 points, composed of five parts:

Module Points Moral Quality (S1) 15 points Academic Quality (S2) 65 points Physical Quality (S3) 8 points Aesthetic Quality (S4) 6 points Labor Quality (S5) 6 points

An additional deduction item S0 is compiled by the department and class based on daily management records.

docs.title: Moral Quality (15 Points)
docs.text:
Moral score = Teacher evaluation (D1, 4 points) + Peer evaluation (D2, 4 points) + Moral scoring (D3, 7 points)

Part Description Teacher Evaluation (D1) Counselors, class teachers, etc. rate on a scale of Excellent/Good/Average/Poor, scoring 4/3/2/1 points respectively Peer Evaluation (D2) Youth University Study completion rate of 100% adds 2 points, 95% adds 1 point, 90% adds 0.5 points; class peer evaluation scores 2/1.5 points for top 30%/60% ranking, 1 point for the rest Moral Scoring (D3) Base score of 2 points (4 points for returning veterans), 2.5 points for serving the collective, other bonus items (self-study, party/league activities, blood donation, etc.)

docs.title: Academic Quality (65 Points)
docs.text:
Academic score = Academic performance (Z1) + Innovation and entrepreneurship score (Z2, capped at 6 points cumulative)

  • Academic performance: Primarily based on exam course grades
  • Innovation and entrepreneurship score: Scored according to the "Qingdao University Undergraduate Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice Credit Scoring Standards." For details, see Innovation Practice Credits

docs.title: Physical Quality (8 Points)
docs.text:
Physical score = Physical fitness test (T1, 4 points) + Campus health run (T2, 2 points) + Extracurricular physical activities (T3, 2 points)

  • T1/T2 data are provided by the School of Physical Education; health run scores are proportional to distance (e.g., running 30km out of a 60km requirement earns half credit)
  • Extracurricular physical activities: Department-level participation adds 0.2 points, university-level adds 0.2 points, award winners earn bonus points by level, capped at 2 points cumulative

docs.title: Aesthetic Quality (6 Points)
docs.text:
Aesthetic score = Art practice (M1, 2 points) + Cultural practice (M2, 2 points) + Classic reading (M3, 2 points)

  • Department-level art/cultural practice: 0.5 points per participation, 1 point per award; university-level and above: 1 point per participation, 2 points per award, capped at 2 points cumulative
  • Classic reading: Completing 2 classic books per semester, submitting a reading reflection earns 1 point per piece, book club sharing earns 0.5 points per session, capped at 2 points cumulative

docs.title: Labor Quality (6 Points)
docs.text:
Labor score = Daily labor (L1, 3 points) + Social practice (L2, 3 points)

Part Description Daily Labor (L1) Dormitory hygiene averages: 95+ points earns 2.5 points, 90–94 earns 2 points, 85–89 earns 1 point, 80–84 earns 0.5 points, below 80 earns 0 points; university-level or above commendations add 0.5 points per instance, capped at 3 points cumulative Social Practice (L2) University/department-organized social practice: 0.5 points per participation; university-level commendation 2 points per instance, department-level 1 point per instance; volunteer activities: 0.2 points per hour, semester cap of 1 point

docs.title: Deduction Item (S0)
docs.text: Violations of dormitory management regulations resulting in criticism or adverse impact: 0.2 points per instance, 0.4 for the second instance, 0.8 for the third, doubling each time.

docs.title: General Rules
docs.text:
• Within the same semester, the same achievement (work, grade, project, deed, etc.) receiving awards at different levels is counted only at the highest score, with no cumulative scoring
  • All bonus items require submitting certificate copies; award certificates must bear the "Qingdao University" or department seal to be valid
  • Team projects: For those with ranked positions, the first-ranked person receives full points, others receive 1/2; for unranked team projects, all members receive full points
  • Fraud during the comprehensive assessment process results in a moral score of zero
  • Comprehensive scores are​保留​ to two decimal places

docs.title: Course Selection Guide
docs.text:
Policy Basis

This page is compiled from the "Qingdao University Undergraduate-Graduate Integrated Teaching Management Platform Course Selection Operation Guide." The original document contains interface screenshots; only text steps are retained here.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
• Login address: http://xjw.qdu.edu.cn/
  • It is recommended to use a desktop computer; mobile devices may experience missing page elements
  • Username is your student ID; password is your Smart Campus password
  • Forgotten password: Log in to Smart Campus to reset via bound mobile phone SMS, or contact Smart Campus at 0532-85955678

docs.title: Entering Course Selection
docs.text:
1. After logging in, click the "Course Selection Center" icon, or navigate from the left menu: Training Management → Course Management → Student Course Selection Center
  2. Confirm the course selection round name and start time, then click "Enter Course Selection" in the operation column

docs.title: Course Selection Center Interface
docs.text:
Area Function Area 1 Schedule of selected courses (does not refresh immediately after selection; click "Default Period Mode" in the upper left corner to manually refresh) Area 2 Selected credit statistics (click "Refresh" to manually update) Area 3 Available course tabs

Area 3 contains three tabs:

  • Course Selection Credit Status: Maximum course selection credit limit for the current semester and current selections
  • Professional Elective Course Selection: Elective courses within your major's current semester plan
  • General Elective Course Selection: All university-wide general elective courses offered this semester

docs.title: Course Selection and Withdrawal
docs.text:
• The system has pre-arranged required courses within your plan. First click "View Selection Results and Withdraw" to verify the pre-arranged results
  • Selecting courses: Based on the class schedule in the system, search for courses in the "Professional Elective Course Selection" or "General Elective Course Selection" tab, then click [Select] on the corresponding row
  • Withdrawing from courses: In "Selection Results," select the course and click [Withdraw] on the corresponding row
  • After completing course selection, click the "Safe Exit Course Selection" button in the upper right corner to exit the course selection interface

docs.title: Viewing Class Schedule
docs.text:
• On the system homepage, click [My Schedule] → [Semester Theory Schedule]
  • The schedule is divided into two parts: courses with time and location shown in each period slot; courses without time and location shown in the notes

docs.title: Freshman English Placement Exam
docs.text: As per tradition, there is an English placement exam after school starts, covering listening and reading. It is somewhat difficult, harder than the gaokao. Question types are similar to CET-4, serving as a placement test and allocation of spots for the College English Competition. If you have the capacity, it's worth preparing in advance. Graduate students also take this exam; a high score can exempt you from graduate English courses.

docs.title: CET-4 and CET-6 Exams
docs.text:
• You can register for CET-4 in the spring semester of freshman year
  • CET-6 can be taken after passing CET-4; if you miss one exam, you cannot register for the next one and must wait until the one after that. Fushan test centers for CET-4 are hard to secure, and CET-6 spots are even harder
  • The listening section requires a radio; the university distributes them uniformly (pre-order through the orientation system), or you can purchase your own

docs.title: Final Exams
docs.text:
• The last two weeks of each semester are exam weeks
  • Multiple classes take exams in the same classroom, seated every other seat, generally by student ID number, though some proctors don't enforce this
  • Final exam grades are linked to various evaluations and honors

docs.title: Exam Discipline
docs.text:
Cheating is Strictly Prohibited

Failing an exam allows for a makeup exam, but if cheating is caught by an inspector, you will face disciplinary action with serious consequences! Students who applied for a deferred exam may take the makeup exam.

According to the "Shandong Province Regular Higher Education Credit System Management Regulations": - Absent from exam: Students may not participate in the makeup or deferred exam for the relevant course and can only retake it - A student who fails to attend the normal course examination without valid reason is considered absent from the exam

docs.title: Exam Rankings
docs.text:
• Exam year rankings are only within your own major
  • Some grade requirements consider class proportions

docs.title: Failing a Course and Makeup Exams
docs.text: Situation Handling First time failing A makeup exam is arranged at the beginning of the new semester; passing the makeup exam records only 60 points in your file Failing the makeup exam Must retake the course, paying the course fee again and studying with the next cohort of students Makeup exam opportunity You only get one makeup exam chance per failure

docs.title: Consequences of Failing
docs.text:
Failing Has Serious Consequences

  • Affects postgraduate recommendation eligibility
  • Affects scholarship evaluation
  • Affects party membership and other evaluation activities
  • Affects student council elections
  • Recorded in your personal file, impacting future employment

docs.title: Scholarships
docs.text:
Scholarships are evaluated at the beginning of each semester for the previous semester, ranked by comprehensive assessment scores, with higher scores having priority.

Scholarship Type Description First-Class Scholarship Top 5% in comprehensive assessment ranking Second-Class Scholarship Top 15% in comprehensive assessment ranking Third-Class Scholarship Top 30% in comprehensive assessment ranking Progress Scholarship Top ranking improvement within the department

Scholarship quotas are allocated by the department to each grade, then distributed by department enrollment proportions.

docs.title: Postgraduate Recommendation (Exemption from Entrance Exam)
docs.text:
Postgraduate recommendation refers to recommending outstanding graduating undergraduates for exemption from the national graduate entrance exam (abbreviated as "tuimian"), directly entering the re-examination phase. Qingdao University's recommendation process follows the "Qingdao University Implementation Measures for Recommending Outstanding Graduating Undergraduates for Exemption from Graduate Entrance Examination" (Document No. QDU-Jiao [2021] 21), with the Academic Affairs Office publishing annual notices each September. The following content is compiled based on the 2025 recommendation work documents.

How many postgraduate recommendation spots are there? Quotas are not set by a fixed proportion but are allocated by the university based on each school's graduating class size, major construction status, teaching achievement awards, and student advanced study rates, distributed to departments each year, then further distributed to majors based on graduating class enrollment and training quality. To learn your major's specific quota, check the "Recommendation Implementation Plan" published by your department in early September.

docs.title: Recommendation Categories
docs.text:
Category Description Regular Recommendation Open to most students, recommended based on comprehensive score ranking Counselor Recommendation Plan For students with the qualities and willingness to serve as student counselors, following the full-time counselor selection process

Each student may only obtain one category of recommendation eligibility and cannot apply for multiple.

docs.title: Basic Requirements (Hard Threshold)
docs.text:
1. Current university graduating undergraduate enrolled in the national regular full-time undergraduate admissions plan (excluding college-to-university transfers and second bachelor's degrees)
  2. Moral quality assessment score of "good" or above, with no record of violations or disciplinary actions
  3. Completed and passed all courses specified in the professional training plan for the corresponding year, with no failing grades in required courses

Failing a Required Course = Automatic Disqualification

If even one required course has a failing record, you cannot apply for postgraduate recommendation. Failing not only affects evaluations but is also a veto criterion for postgraduate recommendation.

docs.title: Academic and Language Requirements for Regular Recommendations
docs.text:
Grade Ranking (Exam Course Average GPA):

Student Type Ranking Requirement Regular Students 4-year programs: top three years; 5-year programs: top four years. Exam course average GPA ranking no lower than top 30% of the major Innovation Experiment Classes, Excellence Talent Plan Majors May be relaxed to top 40% Students with genuine special academic expertise May be relaxed to top 50%

Language Requirements:

Student Type Requirement Non-foreign language majors (English) CET-6 score ≥ 426, or IELTS ≥ 6 / TOEFL ≥ 80 Non-foreign language majors (other languages) Corresponding language CET-4 ≥ 80, or CET-6 ≥ 60 Foreign language majors Passing the corresponding language professional CET-4 exam Arts and sports majors CET-4 score ≥ 426

docs.title: How Comprehensive Score Is Calculated (Core)
docs.text:
Rankings are based on comprehensive score, composed of academic performance and comprehensive development quality assessment score:

Comprehensive Score = Academic Performance × 90% + Comprehensive Development Quality Assessment Score × 10%

  • Academic Performance: All exam course grades during enrollment, out of 100 points. Accounting for 90%, this is decisive.
  • Comprehensive Development Quality Assessment Score: Out of 100 points, composed of social practice and special academic expertise, accounting for 10%.

Grades Are King

Comprehensive development accounts for at most 10%, and the conditions for earning high scores are stringent (see below). For most students, ranking among the top in exam course grades is the most reliable path to postgraduate recommendation. Competitions and volunteer work are merely bonuses.

docs.title: Comprehensive Development Quality Assessment Components (Out of 100)
docs.text:
Section Weight Sub-items Social Practice 30% Military service (10%), volunteer service (10%), international organization internships (10%) Special Academic Expertise 70% "Internet+" competition direct bonus, Challenge Cup (20%), other authoritative competitions (25%), research achievements (25%)

Each sub-item is out of 100 points, converted by weight and summed; each sub-item may accumulate at most three representative works, with the same achievement/award counted only at the highest level without duplication. Scores exceeding 100 are capped at 100.

  • Social Practice: Military service of 2+ years scores 80 points, "Outstanding Soldier" title scores 100 points; national/provincial "Most Beautiful Volunteer," "Outstanding Youth Volunteer," "Three Goes to the Countryside" outstanding individuals, etc. scored by level; international organization internships of 3+ months earn points.
  • "Internet+" Competition: A direct bonus item, converted at 70% and added to the special academic expertise category. National gold awards for top 3 positions: 100/80/60 points; silver: 80/60/40; bronze: 60/40/20.
  • Challenge Cup: Converted at 20%. National gold awards for top 3: 100/80/60 points; silver: 80/60/40; bronze: 60/40/20.
  • Other Authoritative Competitions: Converted at 25%. Based on the Chinese Higher Education Society's "National Ordinary University Student Competition Ranking" for the recommendation year; top awards for competitions on the ranking list capped at 50 points, unlisted competitions capped at 40 points. Scoring standards are set by each department.
  • Research Achievements: Converted at 25%. Papers must be published with Qingdao University as the first author institution and the student as independent or first author. Scoring standards are set by each department.

How are key team members determined for team competitions? For individual competitions, participants are key members; for team competitions where positions can be identified, the top 3 positions are taken with decreasing scores; for team competitions where positions cannot be identified, all team members share equally. The total points for all key team members must not exceed 2.4 times that of individual competition participants at the same level.

docs.title: Special Academic Expertise Defense
docs.text: Students with special academic expertise must submit the "Special Academic Expertise Review and Appraisal Form" and supporting materials, participating in a public defense organized by the department (typically no fewer than 5 experts, associate professor rank or above). The entire defense is audio and video recorded, with results publicly announced. Those who do not pass the review or defense will not have their special academic expertise score counted.

docs.title: Recommendation Work Process (Using 2025 as an Example)
docs.text: Time Step Early September University publishes recommendation notice; department announces implementation plan (including major quotas) Before September 11 Department submits recommendation work plan and working group list September 9–18 Students submit application forms and materials; those with special expertise participate in defense; department reviews, determines candidates, and publicly announces for 7 days September 19–24 University reviews materials, leadership group deliberates and announces September 25–26 Recommendation list submitted to the Ministry of Education's recommendation system

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• When higher-ranked students waive their recommendation quota, they must sign a written waiver, and quotas are filled sequentially by comprehensive score ranking
  • Those who have obtained recommendation eligibility but receive disciplinary action or cannot graduate normally before graduation will have their qualification revoked by the university and reported to the Ministry of Education
  • Fabrication of application materials results in immediate disqualification upon discovery and strict disciplinary action
  • Those with immediate family members participating in the current year's selection must proactively​回避​; non-immediate family members must proactively report
  • The recommendation process involves department and university-level public announcements, subject to supervision by the university's Discipline Inspection Commission (Supervision Office) throughout the process, with real-name reporting accepted

docs.title: Physical Education Classes and Fitness Tests
docs.text:
• Physical education classes are once per week
  • Each semester has fitness tests and final exams
  • Physical education classes carry credits; failing requires a makeup exam

docs.title: Physical Education Activity Selection
docs.text: Gender Available Activities Male Soccer, basketball, track and field, volleyball, etc. Female Aerobics, volleyball, badminton, basketball, track and field, table tennis, etc.

docs.title: Fitness Test Standards

docs.title: Sports Meet
docs.text:
The university sports meet is generally held in April, with events including:

  • Men's: 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 1500m, 5000m, 110m hurdles, relay, high jump, long jump, triple jump, shot put, discus, javelin
  • Women's: 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 1500m, 3000m, 100m hurdles, relay, high jump, long jump, triple jump, shot put, discus, javelin
  • Team events: Tug of war, 1-minute rope skipping, shuttle relay, etc.

docs.title: Radio
docs.text: English exams (including CET-4 and CET-6) require a radio. The university distributes them uniformly (pre-order through the orientation system), or you can purchase your own. You don't need an expensive one, but avoid one that's prone to problems.

docs.title: Class Schedule Lookup
docs.text:
• Qingdao University Academic Affairs Office website: Search "QDU Academic Affairs" on Baidu, log in to check
  • WeChat official account "Qingxiao Zhu": Can check your class schedule synchronously
  • Freshman class schedules become available in the academic affairs system during the late military training period

docs.title: Grade Lookup
docs.text: Grades for all courses and personal ranking information can be queried through the Qingdao University Academic Affairs System.

docs.title: Examination Management Regulations
docs.text:
Policy Basis

This page is compiled from the "Qingdao University Examination Management Regulations" (Document No. QDU-Jiao [2014] 25), effective from the fall semester of 2014. If there are any changes, please refer to the latest documents from the Academic Affairs Office.

docs.title: Grade Composition
docs.text:
• Course overall grade = Regular assessment (midterm, class discussions, quizzes, experiments, assignments, papers, attendance, etc.) + Final exam grade; generally, regular assessment accounts for 20% and the final exam for 80%
  • Teaching units may adjust the grade assessment ratio based on actual course conditions, subject to filing with the Academic Affairs Office before implementation
  • All course assessments use a 100-point scale; 60 points or above is required to earn credits

docs.title: Violations and Absence from Exams
docs.text:
• If a student violates exam rules, cheats, or is absent from an exam, the exam paper score is recorded as zero, and this is noted on the official grade report
  • Arriving more than 15 minutes late prohibits participation in the exam; the course is treated as an absence
  • 30 minutes after the exam begins, students may leave the exam room only with the proctor's permission

docs.title: Exam Room Rules
docs.text:
• Arrive 15 minutes early with valid identification, sit in the designated seat, and place your ID on the desk for verification
  • Those who have lost their identification must have their department issue a written certificate (with photo, counselor's signature, and department seal); otherwise, they cannot take the exam
  • Books, notes, scratch paper,​垫物​, calculators, mobile phones, and other communication devices are not permitted in the exam room (unless the exam has special provisions)
  • If the above items are found on your desk, in your desk compartment, or within arm's reach after the exam begins, they will all be treated as violations
  • Answer sheets must be written in blue or black ink pen or fountain pen; answer sheets are filled in with 2B pencil
  • During the exam, you may not borrow stationery from others without permission; answer sheets and answer paper must not be placed on neighboring desks
  • Peeking, whispering, exchanging secret signals or gestures are strictly prohibited
  • After the exam end signal, you must immediately stop writing; exam papers and scratch paper are placed face-down on the desk and must not be taken out of the exam room
  • Those who submit their papers early must not linger near the exam room or make noise

docs.title: Grade Review
docs.text:
After grades are announced, if a review is needed, you must fill out the "Qingdao University Grade Review Application Form" for approval by the course unit:

Time Item Week 1 Grade review period: Two or more peer experts review; if errors are confirmed, corrections are made on the exam paper with signatures Week 2 Grade correction period: Grades are corrected, and the grading teacher, student, and student's department are notified Week 3 Grade archiving period: The teaching secretary completes grade archiving through the integrated academic affairs system

Makeup exam grades must have review applications submitted within one week of grade announcement, following the above procedure.

docs.title: Innovation Practice Credits
docs.text:
Policy Basis

This page is compiled from the "Qingdao University Undergraduate Innovation Practice Credit Recognition and Management Measures" (Document No. QDU-Jiao [2024] 22), issued on January 17, 2025, replacing the former Document No. QDU-Jiao [2015] 1; scoring standards refer to the "Qingdao University Undergraduate Innovation Practice Credit Scoring Standards" and the "Professional Level Examination Scoring Table." If there are any changes, please refer to the latest documents from the Academic Affairs Office.

Actually, the fact that your driver's license can earn you points isn't the craziest part — the craziest is that writing two Tomato novels can count as passing, since they won't hold you back from graduation over this. In theory, even marriage and divorce certificates could earn you two extra points. (Just kidding, read on for the real rules)

docs.title: What Is This
docs.text:
Innovation practice credits refer to the credits earned by undergraduates during their enrollment period through achieving results in academic competitions, professional qualification exams, innovation and entrepreneurship training projects, publishing papers or works, scientific research, inventions, academic exchanges, professional certification, and entrepreneurial practice, which are recognized by the university. They serve as the grade basis for the university's required "Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice" course (3 credits).

  • Applied for and recognized through the university's "Second Classroom" online platform, with results recorded on the "Second Classroom Transcript"
  • Students who do not earn at least 3 points will not meet graduation requirements ("Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice" is a required course, 3 credits)
  • These are the 3 credits under the "Innovation and Entrepreneurship" category of the Second Classroom, independent of and non-duplicative with other Second Classroom modules

docs.title: Significance and Purpose
docs.text:
• National Initiative: Innovation and entrepreneurship education is a key direction for national higher education reform. The State Council and Ministry of Education have issued multiple directives supporting student innovation and entrepreneurship training projects; innovation practice credits are the practical implementation
  • Driving Growth: Encouraging students to apply classroom knowledge to real-world scenarios such as competitions, research, and entrepreneurship, enhancing innovative spirit, entrepreneurial awareness, and practical capabilities
  • Graduation Necessity: It is a clearly defined required course; failing to earn 3 credits affects graduation — it's a "must-achieve" hard credit
  • Postgraduate Recommendation Bonus: Achievements such as competition awards, published papers, patents, and software copyrights not only count toward Second Classroom scoring but also serve as important credentials for postgraduate recommendation and scholarship evaluation

docs.title: Grade Conversion
docs.text:
In the graduation semester, based on the total points recognized on the "Second Classroom" platform, the course grade for "Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice" (required course, 3 credits) is recorded:

Recognized Total Points Course Grade 10 or above 100 8 or above but less than 10 95 5 or above but less than 8 90 3 or above but less than 5 85 Less than 3 55

docs.title: Recognition Process
docs.text:
1. The student fills out the Innovation Practice Credit application form and submits valid proof materials (certificates, papers, project completion certificates, etc.) for innovation and entrepreneurship achievements to their department
  2. The department reviews the application materials and recognizes the corresponding points based on the content and level of the achievements
  3. The department uploads the recognized data to the "Second Classroom" online platform, recording it on your "Second Classroom Transcript"
  4. In the graduation semester, based on the total recognized points, the department enters the "Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice" course grade

Each department may add its own innovation and entrepreneurship practice achievement items based on its disciplinary characteristics, subject to approval by the Academic Affairs Office. Contact: School of Innovation and Entrepreneurship (phone 85957378).

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: Can language and computer certificates be stacked? A: No. Certificates of the same type are only counted at the highest point level, with no cumulative scoring.

Q: Can a driver's license earn points? A: No. A driver's license is not within the scope of "National Vocational Skills Standards Directory" professional qualifications, nor does it belong to the above scoring standards. Although online jokes say a driver's license can earn points, Qingdao University's current documents do not include this item.

Q: If I won multiple awards in the same competition, how is it calculated? A: The same competition in the same year is only counted once at the highest award level.

Q: How are team award points distributed? A: The team leader or first-ranked member receives double points; other members receive single points.

Q: What counts as a "national-level registration qualification certificate"? A: This refers to professional qualifications listed in the "National Vocational Skills Standards Directory," certificates issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, verifiable on the Vocational Skills Certification Query System (http://zscx.osta.org.cn); "professional qualification certificates" are issued by industry administrative departments or industry associations.

Q: What counts as a core journal? A: Each department determines journal classification standards based on its own disciplinary characteristics. Please consult your department's academic affairs office for specifics.

Integrity Reminder

Those who fabricate information during the application and recognition process will have their recognized points revoked and be subject to strict disciplinary action per regulations. You can earn points gradually, but once your credibility is compromised, it becomes a serious problem.

docs.title: Party Membership
docs.text: Qingdao University's Party member development process is uniformly arranged by the university, with slight variations between departments. The following outlines the university's unified process for students interested in joining the Party.

docs.title: Overall Process
docs.text:
Submit Party membership application → Selected as Party activist → Selected as development target → Party school training and examination → Probationary Party member → Full Party member

  • Submit Party membership application: After one year, upon passing the department-organized Party Constitution examination, you are selected as a Party activist
  • Selected as development target: After being a Party activist for one year, you may be selected as a development target
  • Party school training: Once confirmed as a development target, you participate in unified Party school training (short-term training of 24 credit hours, of which 12 are organized by the department and 12 are studied collectively at the Qingdao University Theater)
  • Organizational interview: After passing the examination, the university Party committee organizes unified interviews for that semester's development targets, primarily questioning on Party membership motivation and Party theory knowledge
  • Probationary Party member: Three months after becoming a development target, the university organizes a Party Constitution examination; upon passing and public announcement of results, you become a probationary Party member
  • Full Party member: One-year probation period, after which you become a full Party member

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
• Starting from the spring semester of freshman year, Party activists are selected each semester
  • Starting from the fall semester of junior year, development targets may be selected (must have been a Party activist for one year)
  • Fall and spring semesters of junior year, and fall and spring semesters of senior year — four rounds of development target selection total. Using the example of being selected as a development target in the fall of junior year: this counts as the "first batch," requiring you to have been selected as a Party activist before the fall of sophomore year (so being in the first or second batch of activists makes no difference)
  • After being confirmed as a development target, after learning and examinations, you can become a probationary Party member in about three months; after the one-year probation period, you become a full member
  • The first batch typically becomes full members around December of junior year; the second batch usually becomes full members right before graduation
  • The earliest you can become a full Party member is the fall semester of senior year; the latest is being selected as a development target in the spring semester of senior year and becoming a probationary member right before graduation

docs.title: Ideological Reports
docs.text:
After being selected as a Party activist, you must submit one ideological report per quarter until you are selected as a development target.

  • If you are selected as an activist early and successfully become a development target in the fall of junior year, you only need about 4 reports
  • If you become an activist in the spring of freshman year and don't become a development target until the spring of senior year, you'll need to write about 12 reports

docs.title: Party Constitution Examination
docs.text:
• Selection as a Party activist requires passing the department-organized Party Constitution examination; at the development target stage, the university also organizes Party Constitution examinations, with question types basically consistent with the department's
  • Question types include fill-in-the-blank, multiple choice, short answer, and essay questions (subjective questions worth approximately 20 points)
  • 60 points is passing; failing means losing the chance to become a probationary Party member this round
  • After passing the examination, results are publicly announced, and you become a probationary Party member

docs.title: Training Classes
docs.text: Once confirmed as a development target, you participate in unified Party school training organized by the university: short-term training of 24 credit hours, of which 12 are organized by the department and 12 are studied collectively at the Qingdao University Theater. The university organizes two development target training classes each year (Session 63 was held on April 27, 2024; by August 2026, Session 67 has been organized; Session 68 will be organized around October 2026, and so on).

docs.title: Organizational Transfer
docs.text:
• When transferring Party activist status to another university, community, or Party organization, your activist status may not necessarily be recognized; generally, you need to restart the development process
  • Similarly, transferring development target status to another location may also not be recognized
  • If you have already become a probationary Party member before graduation, there is no impact: becoming a full member does not consume the receiving organization's development quota, and you can inherit the status and become a full member on schedule, but you'll need to return to the university to retrieve your files

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Academic performance is an important condition for selection: good grades are the primary condition, but not sufficient on their own. Generally, a ranking in the top 30% is required (class committee members have a minimum threshold of top 50%)
  • To aim for becoming a full Party member before graduation, it is generally recommended to also have experience as a deputy class monitor or above, or student council leadership, while also accumulating volunteer service hours
  • Undergraduates generally have four semesters (fall and spring of junior year, fall and spring of senior year) with opportunities to be selected as probationary and full Party members before graduation

docs.title: Second Classroom
docs.text:
Policy Basis

This page is compiled from the university's "Second Classroom Transcript" system implementation measures (including participation hour allocations, participation/exchange and approval operation instructions). If there are any changes, please refer to the latest documents from the Youth League Committee.

docs.title: What is the Second Classroom
docs.text:
The Second Classroom is a comprehensive educational system that complements the "First Classroom" (in-class course instruction). While the First Classroom teaches knowledge, the Second Classroom builds skills — referring to various extracurricular activities you participate in outside of class: ideological guidance, labor practice, cultural and sports activities, innovation and entrepreneurship training, physical exercise, growth portfolios, and more.

At Qingdao University, the Second Classroom is not an optional "extracurricular activity" but a mandatory requirement linked to graduation: since the fall semester of 2024, the university has implemented the "Second Classroom Transcript" system, requiring undergraduates to complete 6 Second Classroom credits, otherwise they will not meet graduation requirements.

docs.title: Its Significance and Purpose
docs.text:
• Implementing National Requirements: Responding to the era's demand to "emphasize and strengthen Second Classroom construction," it is an in-depth exploration of quality education in the new era and an inheritance and innovation of the "College Student Quality Development Plan" [Document No. CYL-Fa [2018] 5]
  • Recording the Growth Process: Through a smart platform, activities you participate in and achievements you gain outside the classroom become recordable, assessable, measurable, and presentable on your "Second Classroom Transcript"
  • Guiding Holistic Student Development: Guiding balanced growth across six dimensions — ideological and political, labor, cultural and sports, innovation and entrepreneurship, physical education, and growth portfolio — so you're not just a "problem-solving machine"
  • Linked to Service and Support: The transcript becomes an important reference for comprehensive quality assessment, scholarship evaluation, party membership recommendation, youth league membership recommendation, postgraduate recommendation, and employment recommendation during your time at the university. At graduation, the transcript is included in your personal file as supporting documentation for job applications and further studies [Document No. CYL-Fa [2018] 5; Article 20 of the New Second Classroom System]

In short: The First Classroom helps you graduate, and the Second Classroom helps you look more "complete" when graduating, while also boosting your scholarship and postgraduate recommendation applications.

docs.title: Six Course Categories
docs.text:
The Second Classroom offers 6 categories, divided into required and elective:

Category Type Examples Ideological Guidance Required Party classes, Youth League school, Youth Marxist Training Program, themed education, military service, National Flag Guard, etc. Labor Practice Required Campus labor, winter/summer social practice, volunteer service, internship training, "Blue Bird Plan," etc. Cultural and Sports Activities Required Art performances, speeches and debates, cultural and arts festivals, various sports competitions, etc. Innovation and Entrepreneurship Required Academic competitions, innovation and entrepreneurship training projects, papers, patents and software copyrights, professional qualifications, entrepreneurial practice, etc. Physical Education Required Junior and senior year PE classes, physical fitness tests, specialized sports skills (Tai Chi, etc.) Growth Portfolio Optional Student council, clubs, class and league organization leadership positions

docs.title: Second Classroom System (Hours + Credits)
docs.text: The Second Classroom uses an "hour accumulation + credit recognition" system: you accumulate hours by participating in activities, and once you have enough, you can convert them into credits. You must earn all credits to graduate.

docs.title: How Hours Are Categorized
docs.text:
Hours come in two types:

  • Participation Hours: Automatically recorded by the system after you register for an activity, check in on-site, and pass the organizer's review
  • Exchange Hours: Earned by applying to exchange your award certificates and honors each semester (typically recognized once in the first month of each semester, with results publicly announced for 3 days)

Key rules:

  • The same content is counted only at the maximum hour level, with no duplicate accumulation
  • Team activities: The first-ranked person (leader) receives full hours, other members receive half the hours (rounded up to 0.5 if less)
  • Activity level is based on the level of the signing and stamping unit

docs.title: How Credits Are Awarded
docs.text:
The Second Classroom totals 6 credits, divided into four modules:

Module Credits Recognizing Unit Development and Training (Ideological Guidance + Cultural and Sports + Growth Portfolio) 1 credit Youth League Committee Labor Practice 1 credit Youth League Committee Innovation and Entrepreneurship 3 credits School of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Physical Education 1 credit School of Physical Education

Among these, the 3 Innovation and Entrepreneurship credits are what we commonly call innovation practice credits. For details on how to earn these 3 credits, see the Innovation Practice Credits Column.

docs.title: Hour Requirements
docs.text:
The Development and Training and Labor Practice modules total 2 credits, requiring completion of no fewer than 64 hours of corresponding activities:

  • Required items: Labor Practice must be at least 32 hours (of which campus public area labor practice must be at least 6 hours)
  • Ideological Guidance and Cultural and Sports Activities each require no fewer than 4 hours
  • The combined total of Ideological Guidance + Cultural and Sports Activities + Growth Portfolio must be no fewer than 32 hours

docs.title: How Hours Convert to Grades
docs.text:
Hours from Labor Practice and Development and Training are converted to scores using standard criteria and entered into the academic affairs system:

Hours Converted Score Less than 32 hours 55 points Exactly 32 hours 85 points More than 32 but no more than 45 hours 90 points More than 45 hours 95 points

docs.title: Quick Reference: Hour Allocation Standards (Exchange Hour Reference)
docs.text:
Accumulating hours mainly comes from participating in activities, but you can also "exchange" hours using honors, certificates, and leadership positions. Common exchange standards:

Item Exchange Hours National / Provincial / Municipal / University / Department Level Honors 10 / 8 / 6 / 4 / 2 University-level or above volunteer service / social practice key team approval Additional 4 / 3 / 2 Student Military Training Instructor 6 per time Campus public area labor practice per session 2 Classroom/laboratory cleaning duty (one full semester) 6 University / Department lectures, themed education activities 2 / 1 University / Department organizers, staff 3 / 2 National competition awards (1st, 2nd, 3rd prize, and excellence award) 10 / 8 / 6 / 5 Provincial competition awards 7 / 6 / 5 / 4 Municipal and department-level competition awards Proportionally decreasing Class monitor, Youth League secretary (one year term with passing evaluation) 8

For the complete and precise hour allocation table, refer to the "Qingdao University Second Classroom Transcript Hour Allocation Table." Rules follow the latest annual documents.

docs.title: How to Participate? Platform Operation Guide
docs.text: Qingdao University's "Second Classroom" operates on a smart platform, accessible via both computer and mobile phone.

docs.title: Platform Access
docs.text:
Platform Method Desktop Visit http://ehall.qdu.edu.cn, log in and click "Youth League Committee System" in the "Service Hall" Mobile Enterprise WeChat Workbench → "Smart Youth League"
  • Username: Student ID for students, Employee ID for staff
  • Initial Password: Last 10 digits of your ID card
  • The account is the same as the Smart Campus account; if forgotten, you can reset via bound mobile phone or call 0532-85955678 for customer service

docs.title: Participation Hours (Activity) Process
docs.text:
1. The activity organizer publishes the activity on the platform and sets the hours
  2. The administrator reviews and approves
  3. You register online (registration closes when spots are filled)
  4. Arrive at the venue — mobile phone QR code scan + location check-in
  5. After the activity ends, the organizer submits verification (within 7 days of activity completion), and the system automatically records the hours

Note: Once an activity has started or the registration period has passed, registration cannot be canceled; remember to check in during the activity period, otherwise participation will not count.

docs.title: Exchange Hours (Certificates and Honors) Process
docs.text:
1. The student enters "Credit Recognition Management" and clicks "Apply"
  2. Select criteria → Fill in application information (all required fields must be completed)
  3. Submit (approval processes differ by type)
  4. After review by the Youth League branch, department-level leadership review, 3-day public announcement, and university-level filing, hours are recorded

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: What happens if I don't accumulate enough Second Classroom hours? A: Undergraduates must complete 6 credits by the end of the seventh semester (ninth semester for 5-year programs). These 6 credits are a mandatory graduation requirement. Graduates who do not meet the requirement can make up credits by participating in designated university/department activities before graduation.

Q: Can hours from different award-winning activities be counted multiple times? A: No. The same activity and the same honor are only counted at the maximum level, with no duplicate accumulation.

Q: How are hours distributed for team awards? A: The leader (first position) receives full hours; other members receive half, rounded up to 0.5 if less.

Q: What if I fabricate information in my application? A: Once verified, your personal registration account will be frozen for one semester, and you will be subject to disciplinary action per regulations. Integrity is very important!

Q: What if I go abroad for exchange, join the military, or take a leave of absence? A: After changes in your enrollment status, Second Classroom work will be handled by your adjusted department. If you apply for early graduation, you can submit your recognition application at the same time.

Important Reminder

The Second Classroom is a mandatory requirement and a hard task for graduation — don't think of it as just an "extra credit activity." You can start accumulating hours and achievements as early as freshman year. Don't wait until junior year to rush out of anxiety. Related information follows the latest university documents.

docs.title: Academic System
docs.text:
Update Pending

Some information on this page may be outdated or unverified. Contributions via GitHub are welcome.

docs.title: Credit System
docs.text: Qingdao University implements a credit-based academic management system. Credits serve as the basic unit for measuring and calculating student workload, with completing the required graduation credits as the primary standard for graduation.

docs.title: Credit Calculation
docs.text:
In principle, the credit calculation for different course types is as follows:

Course Type Credit Calculation Theoretical Courses 1 credit per 16 class hours Laboratory Courses 1 credit per 32 class hours Public Physical Education 1 credit per 32 class hours Intensive Practical Teaching (internships, course projects, graduation projects, etc.) 1 credit per teaching week Distributed Practical Teaching 1 credit per 32 class hours

docs.title: Graduation Credit Requirements
docs.text: Program Duration Minimum Graduation Credits 4-Year Program 160 credits 5-Year Program 220 credits 7-Year Program 300 credits

docs.title: Course Structure
docs.text:
The university offers four categories of courses: - General Education Courses: Including ideological and political theory, college English, physical education, computer fundamentals, and other required public courses, as well as general elective courses - Discipline Foundation Courses: Core foundational courses within the discipline - Professional Courses: Required and elective courses in the major - Special Courses: Innovation and entrepreneurship, social practice, and other specialized courses

Courses are divided into two main categories: required and elective.

docs.title: Course Selection Timing and Methods
docs.text:
• In the first semester of freshman year, you only need to select physical education courses. Notifications typically come around late military training period; other courses are arranged by the Academic Affairs Office, so no self-selection is needed
  • In other semesters, use the Qingdao University Academic Affairs System for online course selection. Specific dates follow Academic Affairs Office notifications
  • After the schedule is finalized, you can log in to "QDU Academic Affairs" (search "QDU Academic Affairs" on Baidu to log in) or use the WeChat official account "Qingxiao Zhu" to check

docs.title: Course Selection Modules
docs.text:
Course selection is divided into multiple modules:

Module Description Required Professional Courses Must be selected; usually pre-arranged by the system Elective Professional Courses Self-selected based on credit requirements and interests General Elective Courses (Core) Must complete 6 credits General Elective Courses (Non-core) Must complete 4 credits Aesthetic Education Courses Must complete 2 credits

Course Selection Advice

Among general elective courses, non-core courses are relatively easier to pass, such as popular courses like "Qingdao Tourism Geography." Freshmen have lower priority in course selection, so it is recommended to choose popular courses in sophomore or junior year. Core courses are mandatory for everyone, and typically the School of Foreign Languages requires two to three core courses.

docs.title: Tuition System
docs.text:
Qingdao University's tuition follows a credit-based fee structure.

  • Except for special programs such as Sino-foreign cooperative education, tuition for other programs is paid once per semester, with the amount related to the number of credits taken that semester
  • The number of courses varies each semester, so the tuition amount also differs each semester
  • Ultimately, over four years of graduation, the total tuition paid is fixed
  • The "average per academic year XXXX yuan" in the admissions brochure is an averaged figure for convenience
  • Generally, tuition for a four-year program is around 25,000 yuan; medical programs are slightly more expensive

docs.title: Class Schedule
docs.text:
• University class schedules are fixed each week
  • Each class is a two-hour lecture
  • Classrooms are generally not fixed, arranged according to the course schedule
  • Instructors may conduct unannounced roll calls, and counselors may also check attendance; attendance is linked to final exam grades

docs.title: On Skipping Classes
docs.text:
Important Reminder

Skipping classes should at least be meaningful. Consequences of getting caught: - Being caught by the instructor will affect your exam grades - Being caught by the counselor means being called to the office for a talk - More than 10 unexcused absences result in a disciplinary warning recorded in your personal file - Absences exceeding 1/3 of total classes will result in disqualification from the final exam for that course

docs.title: Evening Self-Study
docs.text:
• There is no fixed morning self-study
  • Evening self-study is generally required in the first semester of freshman year; it is usually canceled in the second semester due to course arrangements
  • If you choose not to go, just remember to submit a leave request; no one will make things difficult for you

docs.title: Course Arrangement (Example: Computer Science and Other STEM Majors)
docs.text:
Freshman courses typically include:

Semester Main Courses First Semester Advanced Mathematics (I), Discrete Mathematics, College English, Ideological and Political Theory, C Programming, Digital Logic, Introduction to Computer Science Second Semester C++ Programming, Computer Systems Fundamentals, University Physics (III), Linear Algebra, etc.

About Advanced Mathematics and University Physics

Advanced Mathematics and University Physics are each divided into (I), (II), and (III), with varying difficulty levels for different majors: (I) is the hardest, (III) is the easiest.

docs.title: Basic Requirements
docs.text:
• Students must have an exam course average GPA ranking in the top 20% of their major during the first academic year
  • No disciplinary records
  • You may list two preferences

docs.title: Restrictions
docs.text:
• Students admitted to a lower batch of majors cannot transfer to a higher batch
  • Cross-admission-category transfers are not permitted
  • Students in Sino-foreign cooperative programs or university-enterprise cooperative programs cannot transfer to programs with a different cooperative model
  • Students in the Normal (Teacher Education) School can only transfer within normal education programs; students from other schools are not accepted
  • Non-medical students transferring to medical programs must repeat a year
  • Starting from 2023, the target major's admission ranking must not be higher than the original major's, though this has since become more relaxed

docs.title: Admission Rules
docs.text: Receiving departments admit transfer students based on the percentile ranking of their exam course average GPA in their original major. Those not admitted to their first preference may participate in the second preference selection. If neither preference is successful, students remain in their original major.

docs.title: Enrollment Requirements
docs.text:
• After the completion of the first semester of freshman year
  • Exam course average GPA of at least 75
  • No course retakes required
  • Each person may apply for only one major

docs.title: Study and Certification
docs.text:
Item Description Study Duration Typically two years during sophomore and junior years Minor Certificate Awarded upon completing the required credits for the minor program (not an academic degree certificate) Second Degree Awarded to those who meet dual degree requirements (if the same as the primary degree, only one degree certificate is issued)

The Academic Affairs Office announces the list of minor programs offered each spring semester, and each department admits students based on GPA ranking and merit.

docs.title: Second Classroom
docs.text:
Second Classroom refers to a separate educational system complementing the first classroom (in-class course instruction), encompassing various extracurricular activities students participate in outside of class — ideological guidance, labor practice, cultural and sports activities, innovation and entrepreneurship training, physical exercise, growth portfolios, and more. It is not just about "activities" — it is a mandatory requirement linked to graduation: since the fall semester of 2024, Qingdao University has implemented the "Second Classroom Transcript" system, requiring undergraduates to complete 6 Second Classroom credits (of which 3 are innovation practice credits), failing to meet this requirement means not meeting graduation requirements.

  • It is an upgraded version of the "College Student Quality Development Plan," making various extracurricular activities recordable, assessable, measurable, and presentable
  • Participation hours are divided into participation hours (registering for activities, on-site check-in) and exchange hours (earned through certificates and honors)
  • The transcript serves as an important reference for scholarship evaluation, postgraduate recommendation, party membership, and employment recommendations

Detailed rules (how hours are calculated, how credits are awarded, how to operate the platform) have all been compiled:

Related Column

Click here to view the Second Classroom Column.

docs.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship Credits (Innovation Practice Credits)
docs.text:
Hello student, I'm a school administrator. Your essay criticizing current issues was deeply moving, and we feel quite ashamed. To reward you, please tell me your student ID and name, and I'll add innovation practice credits for you right away. (Just kidding, don't take it seriously)

Innovation practice credits are the 3 credits under the "Innovation and Entrepreneurship" category of the Second Classroom, and also a standalone required course ("Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practice," 3 credits). Undergraduates earn credits through achieving results in academic competitions, innovation and entrepreneurship training projects, publishing papers, patents and software copyrights, professional qualification exams, and entrepreneurial practice, which are reviewed and recognized as credits, ultimately converted into course grades. Students who do not earn at least 3 points will not meet graduation requirements — there's no way around it.

  • The higher the points, the higher the course grade (maximum conversion of 100 points)
  • Applied for and recognized through the "Second Classroom" online platform

docs.title: Major Transfer
docs.text:
Content Based on 2023 Policy Documents

This page is compiled from Qingdao University's 2023 major transfer work documents (policy release, registration and admission notices, and grade-specific transfer regulations). Major transfer policies may be adjusted annually, and different grades follow different documents. This page is for reference only. Please refer to the latest notice from the Academic Affairs Office for the current year.

Full of hope, you enrolled in a major that even dogs wouldn't study — but there's still a chance to save yourself (Whether you succeed depends on your grades and whether the receiving department accepts you)

docs.title: One-Sentence Summary
docs.text: Major transfer gives current undergraduates one chance to change their major. Generally, you need good grades, no disciplinary record, no prior major transfers, and must meet the target major's "admissions requirements." Spots are limited every year, and the competition is fierce — start building your grades early if you want to transfer.

docs.title: Policy Basis (By Grade)
docs.text:
Major transfer divides students into "new rules" and "old rules" by grade. Before applying, first determine which document applies to you:

Grade Applicable Document Class of 2021 "Qingdao University Undergraduate Major Transfer Work Management Measures" (Document No. QDU-Jiao [2019] 14) Class of 2022 "Qingdao University Undergraduate Major Transfer Work Regulations" (Document No. QDU-Jiao [2022] 5)

In the 2023 registration notice, the Class of 2021 and Class of 2022 followed the two documents above respectively. Which document applies to your incoming class follows the Academic Affairs Office's notice for that year.

docs.title: Standard Requirements (Using Document No. [2022] 5 as an Example)
docs.text:
• Full-time regular undergraduate second-year students may apply at the beginning of the third semester
  • Excellent academic performance, no failing grades (including retakes)
  • Exam course weighted average GPA ranking in the top 20% of the major

docs.title: Special Circumstances (Not Counting Against Receiving Quota)
docs.text:
The following situations also allow applications and do not count against the receiving plan quota:

  1. Student soldiers resuming studies after military service who wish to change their major
  2. Students whose original major was adjusted or discontinued during their leave of absence, making it impossible to continue in the original major upon return
  3. Students with genuine special difficulties (illness, physical disability, academic difficulties, etc.) making it unsuitable to continue in the original major

docs.title: Who Cannot Apply
docs.text:
The following individuals may not apply for major transfer:

  • Students admitted through special admission categories such as arts, sports, high-level athletes, paired training programs, or comprehensive evaluation
  • Students who have received disciplinary action during their enrollment
  • Students currently on leave of absence or with suspended enrollment status
  • Students who have been enrolled for less than one semester
  • Students who have already transferred majors (each person gets only one chance; once transferred, it's gone)
  • Students who should be dismissed
  • Students transferred from another university
  • Others deemed unsuitable for major transfer by university review

docs.title: Quota and Proportions
docs.text:
• Both receiving and outgoing student numbers for a major must not exceed 10% of that major's current-year enrollment
  • National-level first-class undergraduate program construction sites and majors that have passed professional certification have an outgoing limit of 5%
  • Special circumstance major transfers do not count against the receiving plan quota

docs.title: Gaokao Score Threshold
docs.text:
In principle, your gaokao score must not be lower than the admission cutoff for the same year and source region of the target major:

  1. Shandong Province students: Your gaokao score must not be lower than the minimum admission score for the target major at our university
  2. Students from outside Shandong Province: If the target major had an admission plan in your appropriate region that year, follow the above principle
  3. If the target major had no admission plan, compare the minimum admission scores of your current major and the target major in Shandong Province, ensuring yours is not lower than the target major's
  4. For provinces that have not yet implemented the new gaokao system, refer to item 3 for comparison

Note

This hard threshold was the 2023 policy. It seems to have become more relaxed compared to before. Before transferring, it is recommended to follow the current year's notice and the receiving department's explanation.

docs.title: Admission Method
docs.text:
The primary admission criterion is the percentile ranking of exam course weighted average GPA (the registration system, ranking, and disciplinary records are all synced to the academic affairs system, and the system automatically filters eligibility during registration).

  • The receiving department comprehensively considers your gaokao score, subject selection, and admissions requirements for merit-based admission
  • If a major has only one class with no more than 30 students, and you rank first with an exam course weighted average GPA ≥ 85, admission shall be granted (Class of 2021 document)

docs.title: 2023 Registration Process (For Reference Only)
docs.text:
The following is the actual 2023 timeline, provided for understanding the process only. Timings change each year:

Time Step Early October Academic Affairs Office issues the major transfer registration and admission notice Registration Period (~2 days) Eligible students register online; special circumstances register offline After Registration Outgoing department reviews, receiving department admits Review Period Academic Affairs Office reviews; those with violations are re-admitted Results Announcement Academic Affairs Office announces the proposed admission list (at least 3 working days) Admission Confirmation Accept enrollment; enrollment status transfers to the receiving department

docs.title: How to Register (Online Operation)
docs.text:
Refer to the student operation manual released for the current year. The general steps are as follows:

  1. Log in to the New Academic Affairs System: https://xjw.qdu.edu.cn/
  2. Menu path: Enrollment Status & Grades → Excellent Student Transfer → Major Transfer Application
  3. Click Query to find available majors you can apply to
  4. After confirming you meet the admissions requirements, click Apply, fill in the information and save
  5. Saving indicates a successful application; you can check the review status on this page

The registration system will automatically import your enrollment status, grade ranking, previous transfer records, and disciplinary records. If you don't meet the requirements, you simply cannot register. Fill in information carefully (each application can only be filled once).

docs.title: Admissions Requirements (Target Major's Conditions for Screening You)
docs.text:
In addition to the university's general rules, each department sets its own admissions requirements (see the current year's receiving plan). Common requirements include:

  • Grade Ranking: Such as top 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%
  • Prerequisite Courses: For example, the School of Computer Science may require completion of "Advanced Mathematics I" and "C Programming" with qualifying grades
  • Gaokao Subject Selection: Such as science / physics selection
  • Grade Repetition Requirement: For cross-discipline transfers or insufficient credits, you may be required to repeat a year
  • Language / Certificates: For example, foreign language majors may have strict English grade requirements

Admissions requirements are published each year. Consult the department contacts listed in the current year's plan (each plan includes contacts and phone numbers).

docs.title: What to Do After Successfully Transferring
docs.text:
• Receiving grade is determined by the receiving department; curriculum, program duration, and tuition follow the new major's standards
  • Previously completed courses undergo credit recognition based on the new major's curriculum: courses with identical content and difficulty are directly recognized; similar courses are substituted for new major courses; other courses may be recognized as elective courses
  • You may need to make up required courses not yet taken under the new curriculum
  • The receiving department handles enrollment status, class scheduling, and daily guidance

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: Can sophomores or juniors transfer? A: According to Document No. [2022] 5, primarily second-year students apply at the beginning of the third semester; the 2021 version allowed first and second-year students. Students enrolled for more than one semester or in third year and above generally have no chance. Check the documents for your specific year.

Q: Can I transfer again after having transferred once? A: No. Those who have already transferred cannot apply again. You only get one chance, so choose your target carefully.

Q: Which majors cannot be transferred out of? A: Majors admitted through special categories such as arts, sports, high-level athletes, paired training programs, or comprehensive evaluation cannot be transferred out of.

Q: Can normal education / Sino-foreign cooperative / university-enterprise cooperative students transfer? A: Students in normal education, Sino-foreign cooperative, or university-enterprise cooperative programs can only transfer to programs with the same cooperative model. Publicly funded normal students can adjust within publicly funded normal education. You cannot freely transfer to other training models.

Q: Will I have to repeat a year after transferring? A: It depends. If the major span is large, prerequisite courses haven't been taken, or credits are insufficient, the receiving department will require repeating a year. For example, transferring from a 4-year program to a 5-year medical program, or from humanities to STEM without having taken Advanced Mathematics, usually requires repetition.

Missing the Deadline Means Missing Out

Major transfer registration and review have strict deadlines for each step. Late registration is considered automatic withdrawal; once enrolled after admission, you cannot transfer back. Hesitation is fine, but registering wrong or missing the deadline causes real trouble.

This page is compiled from 2023 major transfer documents. Specific policies follow the Academic Affairs Office's latest annual notice and each department's receiving plan for the current year.

docs.title: Words for You
docs.text:
Foreword

Here are words left by seniors for juniors. Whether it's a word of encouragement, a piece of experience, a pitfall encountered, or something you want to say, you can write it here and pass on this warmth.

docs.title: 炎黄​YH
docs.text:
Everyone's university life has its own meaning. Focus more on value, not on cost. Students who study hard for postgraduate recommendation sacrifice entertainment to gain achievement, while those who slack off with "60 points is enough" sacrifice learning to gain happiness. As long as you don't engage in endless internal friction, and can feel that you were once happy at graduation, that's the best result.

—— ​炎黄​YH

docs.title: 玉环​YH (Class of 2024 Software Engineering)
docs.text:
Make choices carefully, and also be prepared to bear the bitter consequences. And don't regret. Use AI deeply, but absolutely absolutely do not outsource thinking. Students who choose to employ should intern early, work on truly valuable projects, and pay attention to the accumulation of basic knowledge and skills, especially mathematics, algorithms, and 408 professional courses. When looking for jobs, internal referrals and official website applications are much more efficient than BOSS Zhipin. Making more friends and participating in technical communities is beneficial without harm, especially in some relatively vertical fields (such as competitions, certain subdivision industry technologies, etc.). Freshman year might be the most leisurely and happy time in university...

—— ​玉环​YH
